newsitem.title: USA: Sled Dogs resolves problems, revenues on track.
newsitem.headline: Sled Dogs resolves problems, revenues on track.

text.p: Sled Dogs Co said Tuesday it has resolved the supply problems that depressed its fiscal first quarter results and that it is now on track to report net sales for the first half of its fiscal year.
Sales for its fiscal first half ending December 31, 1996, should be significantly ahead of the $876,330 reported for the first six months of fiscal 1996, it said.
The company said that through October 1996, the first four months of its fiscal year, its net sales totaled $525,022.
Sled Dogs markets, makes and distributes Sled Dogs snow skates and related accessories.

"Demand has been strong in U.S. retail channels and in selected international markets, including Canada and Japan," said John Sundet, Sled Dogs president and chief executive officer. "We have recovered from a slow first quarter to achieve our best early-season sales ever with the bulk of the holiday and winter sports season still ahead of us."

Sundet said early-season sales benefited from availability of the company's snow skates in major sporting goods retailers, and marketing programs including a 30-minute infomercial and a website on the Internet.
